_meta.indication: Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active comparator-controlled (ustekinumab), parallel-group trial
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI≥12, IGA≥3, and BSA≥10%) who were candidates for systemic therapy and/or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: IGA 0/1 (clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline) and PASI90
pivotal_trials.n: 567 randomized; co-primary analysis BKZ 320mg Q4W N=321 vs placebo N=83
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1: 270 (84%) BKZ vs 4 (5%) placebo; PASI90: 273 (85%) BKZ vs 4 (5%) placebo; bimekizumab statistically superior to placebo (p<0.001) for both co-primary endpoints

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 4:1 to bimekizumab 320 mg SC Q4W or placebo, with a 16-week Initial Treatment Period followed by a randomized-withdrawal period
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI≥12, IGA≥3, and BSA≥10%) who were candidates for systemic therapy and/or phototherapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints at Week 16: PASI90 response and IGA 0/1 (clear/almost clear with ≥2-grade improvement from baseline)
pivotal_trials.n: 435 randomized; co-primary analysis BKZ 320mg Q4W N=349 vs placebo N=86
pivotal_trials.result: IGA 0/1: 323 (93%) BKZ vs 1 (1%) placebo; PASI90: 317 (91%) BKZ vs 1 (1%) placebo; bimekizumab statistically superior to placebo (p<0.001) for both co-primary endpoints

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥1%): upper respiratory tract infections (15% vs 14% placebo), oral candidiasis (9% vs 0%), headache (3% vs 0%), injection site reactions (3% vs 1%), tinea infections (3% vs 1%), gastroenteritis, herpes simplex infections, acne, folliculitis, and fatigue. Infections occurred in 36% of BIMZELX vs 23% of placebo through 16 weeks.
target_moa: Bimekizumab-bkzx is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively binds human IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-17AF cytokines and inhibits their interaction with the IL-17 receptor complex, thereby inhibiting release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) BLA review; the original BLA (received July 15, 2020) received a Complete Response Letter on May 12, 2022 for GMP facility deficiencies, and the drug was approved on the resubmission received November 21, 2022 based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials (PS0009 and PS0013).

This resubmission is a complete response to the deficiencies outlined in the Complete Response Letter (CRL dated May 12, 2022, Appendix 18.6). The original BLA for bimekizumab (BLA 761151) was submitted on July 15, 2020.

The Applicant submitted data from two adequate and well-controlled trials (PS0009 and PS0013), which provided evidence of the effectiveness of bimekizumab for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adult patients who are candidates for systemic therapy or phototherapy. The trials assessed the changes from Baseline to Week 16 compared to placebo for the co-primary endpoints:

requirement.text: 4268 – 3 Conduct a prospective, registry based observational exposure cohort study that compares the maternal, fetal, and infant outcomes of women exposed to bimekizumab during pregnancy to an unexposed control population. The registry should be designed to detect and record major and minor congenital malformations, spontaneous abortions, stillbirths, elective terminations, small for gestational age, preterm birth, and any other adverse pregnancy outcomes. These outcomes will be assessed throughout pregnancy. Infant outcomes, including effects on postnatal growth and development, neonatal deaths, and infections, will be assessed through at least the first year of life.

requirement.text: 4268 – 6 Conduct a prospective observational study to assess the long-term safety of bimekizumab treatment in US adult patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. Fully ascertain and centrally verify malignancy (including lymphoma), opportunistic infections, reactivation of Hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and serious infections. Other outcomes include hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal events, Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events, and hematologic events. Enroll patients over a 4-year period and plan to follow for a minimum of 8 years from time of enrollment.

citations.quote: 4268 – 6 Conduct a prospective observational study to assess the long-term safety of bimekizumab treatment in US adult patients with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. Fully ascertain and centrally verify malignancy (including lymphoma), opportunistic infections, reactivation of Hepatitis B, tuberculosis, and serious infections. Other outcomes include hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal events (including inflammatory bowel disease, elevated liver enzymes/drug-induced liver injury), Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, and sudden death) and hematologic events. For each adverse-event outcome separately, compare incidence in bimekizumab-treated patients against reference rates internally derived from analyses conducted in patients treated with other chronic systemic treatments for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. Regardless of treatment discontinuation or switch to a different treatment for plaque psoriasis, continue following patients for malignancy outcomes and possibly other adverse events with delayed onset. Enroll a sufficient number of patients to describe the frequency of the adverse events in representative U.S. patients who start treatment with bimekizumab for plaque psoriasis in the setting of routine clinical practice. Implement a plan that uses rigorous, transparent, and verifiable methods to ascertain and characterize safety events that occur during and after treatment with bimekizumab. Enroll patients over a 4-year period and plan to follow for a minimum of 8 years from time of enrollment.
